Here at my observer site in Tok we have gotten 4.5 of snow since last evening at 8 pm_ when the snowfall first began. It is fine grained snow coming down fairly steadily and now fairly heavily. It was fairly thin and sparse last evening but is now heavier. - Katy in Tok.
Moderate to heavy snowfall_ 6 in by 10:50 am_ snowfall rates of about 1.5 to 2 in per hour. Current temp around 30 F with a light wind.

Spotter (Kathy Turk) reported snow began 20:00 AKDT 10/19 and ended 17:00 AKDT 10/20. Additional light snow occurred the morning of the 21st bringing the total to 9.5.
Snow began in earnest Tuesday around 2 pm.

Robyn Russell reporting from 41 Eureka Ave in Hamilton Acres (Fairbanks_ AK). Received about 4.5-5.5 of snow (measuring at different places in my yard). Snow damp_ but not wet. Sun out_ snow melting in sunny spots_ light snow (diamond dust) continuing to fall as of 10/21/26 at 1:50 p.m.
Gusts greater than 35mph with visibility one quarter mile or less from about Noon to 4pm. Maximum gust 48 mph at 3:45pm.
Gusts greater than 35mph with visibility near one quarter mile or less from around 1pm to 4 pm. Max wind gust during this period 48 mph at 2:05pm AKDT.
Six inches of snow fell at Nome Beltz Jr/Sr High School before transitioning to rain as of Friday evening around 6:30 PM.

Multiple public reports of coastal flooding in Hooper Bay with roads inundated_ impacting access to the airfield. Water levels per P-ETSS guidance shows a peak around 4 to 6 feet above the normal high tide line around 2 PM AKDT with gusts up to around 60 mph observed. Water levels are expected to drop to around 2 to 4 feet Friday night into Saturday.

Multiple public reports of coastal flooding in Teller with roads inundated and outlying structures impacted. Water levels per P-ETSS guidance show a peak around 3 to 5 feet above the normal high tide line Friday afternoon through Saturday with gusts up to around 60 mph observed. Water levels are expected to drop to around 2 to 4 feet Sunday into Monday.

Public report of coastal flooding in Wales with roads inundated and outlying structures impacted. Water levels per P-ETSS guidance show a peak around 3 to 5 feet above the normal high tide line Friday through Saturday with gusts up to around 70 mph observed. Water levels are expected to drop to around 2 to 4 feet Sunday into Monday.
